business_scope.primary_industry_name: Interactive Language Education and Automated Tutoring Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European, codified commercial and corporate law under Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 and Código de Comercio)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain-Brazil Cooperation and Investment Facilitation Agreement (when applicable for dual investors)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended by Ley 13/2023, de 21 de noviembre; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo (Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010); Real Decreto 434/2023, de 6 de junio, del Registro de Titularidades Reales; Regulation (EU) 2015/849 (AMLD4) as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5); Law 3/2015 on tax fraud prevention and beneficial ownership transparency.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, good standing, and incumbency of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies register/trade registry of the shareholder's country of establishment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if the origin country is not a Hague Convention member), plus sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copy of all natural-person shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) appearing in the notarial deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national passport/identity authority of each person's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy in the country of origin and, if required by the Spanish notary, Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for the incorporation representative or agent, if the shareholder does not execute the deed personally before the Spanish notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin; countersignature by the Spanish consular office when applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of financial provenance / source of funds for the subscribed share capital (bank reference, funds transfer, or net worth statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Recognized financial institution independent of the incorporating parties
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular legalization under the country-of-origin rules, with sworn Spanish translation if requested by the AML compliance unit

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, administrators, and UBOs against the OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, EU financial sanctions lists, and the domestic list of the Spanish Financial Intelligence Unit (Sepblac). Enhanced due diligence is obligatory for politically exposed persons (PEPs), residents of high-risk third countries, and any UBO with direct or indirect control of 25% or more of the capital or voting rights. Source-of-funds documentation must be evidenced before the notary executes the incorporation deed; any unresolved sanction flag blocks the deed and the UBO registration.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) - Sede Electrónica (www.rmc.es); online denomination certificate applications are processed through the Colegio de Registradores de España portal at www.registradores.org.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must be expressed in Spanish or, if using a co-official language, must also be reproduced in Spanish for the registry index. Accented characters, diacritics, and non-Spanish script are processed through the RMC's transliteration rules; all letters must be replaced with their equivalent Spanish Latin characters. The exact denomination must not be identical or phonetically/orthographically confusingly similar to an existing Spanish or EU registered company name. For an SL, the name must be followed by the expression 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.' (or 'S.L.U.' for sole-member companies).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RMC issues a rejection certificate, the applicant may submit an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) to the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado (DGRN) within one month from the date of notification. The appeal must be filed through the Sede Electrónica del Ministerio de Justicia, identifying the proposed name, the rejection reference, and the legal arguments against the refusal. Alternatively, the applicant may request a new negative-name certificate for a corrected denomination in the RMC online platform; the corrected name can be reserved immediately. A successful appeal or re-application entitles the incorporators to use the name within the remaining validity period or a fresh 90-day validity window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is acceptable for administrative and correspondence purposes for a digital EdTech subscription business, but it cannot be a mere letterbox. Under Art. 23 of the Spanish Capital Companies Act (LSC), the registered office (domicilio social) must coincide with the place where the effective centre of administration or principal establishment is located. If the corporate management, board decisions, and automated service operations are actually managed from Spain, then the virtual office may serve as the formal registered seat provided it hosts real equipment, records, or staff; if no such commercial substance exists, the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) may treat the seat as fictitious and reattribute taxable presence. For a low-risk EdTech company with no physical storefront, a serviced office or business centre is generally accepted, but the company must retain a registered agent and local tax representation to defend the substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a new non-financial digital services company. The administrative and tax inspection rate for newly incorporated SLs in the online subscription sector is below 5% in the first 12 months when no irregular VAT or corporate tax filings occur. However, if the only Spanish presence is a virtual office without personnel, the risk of a targeted on-site verification increases to approximately 15-20%, especially when the company invoices high volumes to related foreign entities or applies preferential tax exemptions.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance certificate (certificación negativa de denominación social) from Registro Mercantil Central
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RMC tariff for online negative-name certification; approximately EUR 10

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial fees for the incorporation public deed (escritura de constitución), including preparation of the articles of association and standard statutory language
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chosen notary belonging to the Colegio Notarial de Madrid / Colegio Notarial de Barcelona as applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff under Real Decreto 1426/1989; prevailing market benchmark for a standard SL deed is EUR 350-550

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the incorporation deed in the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial corresponding to the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee based on the corporate capital and volume of documents under Ley 20/2007 and the Registral Regulations; typical range EUR 150-250

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting and pre-incorporation due diligence fee (bylaws, corporate risk assessment, UBO statement, AML protocols, CSC certification)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Spanish law firm or qualified corporate legal adviser
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a low-risk digital services Spanish SL: EUR 900-1,500 based on time spent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO registration filing and AML compliance consultation in the Registro de Titularidades Reales
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial / Ministry of Justice registry operator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market standard for preparing and submitting the beneficial ownership declaration after the notarial deed; EUR 25-100 registry fee plus legal processing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille/consular legalization of foreign shareholders' constitutional documents, identity documents, and powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority in the country of origin (usually the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or designated court); Spanish consulate for non-Hague countries
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document official fees of USD 20-80; emergent consular rates for legalization; plus sworn translation at EUR 25-60 per page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn Spanish translation of foreign public deeds and apostilled documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator (traductor jurado) appointed by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Professional sworn-translator market tariff of approximately EUR 30-60 per page; calculated for an estimated 3-5 pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) application and documentary handling for foreign administrators/shareholders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de la Policía (Oficina de Extranjería)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official administrative fee from EUR 9-12 for the T790 module plus external handling/agency fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax on Documented Legal Acts (AJD) — 1% of subscribed share capital on the incorporation deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory 1% rate under the consolidated text of the ITP/AJD Law; benchmark capital for an SL is EUR 3,000

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), Articles 20-22 (incorporation), 23-28 (bylaws), 62-64 (registered office), 209-210 (board of directors).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) for name reservation; Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) of the registered office for incorporation filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (Escritura de Constitución) executed before a Spanish notary, followed by registration in the Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum paid-up capital: €3,000 (approx. USD 3,300) as per Article 4 of the Capital Companies Act. The entire capital must be fully subscribed and paid up at incorporation, deposited in a Spanish bank account in the company's name, and the deposit certificate must be attached to the deed. No escrow account is required beyond this initial deposit.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the incorporation deed and bylaws be approved as submitted. That the share capital of €3,000 be fully subscribed and paid up by the founding members, with the bank deposit certificate attached. That the registered office be established at [Address], Madrid, Spain. That [Name] be appointed as Sole Administrator (Administrador Único) with full powers, and [Name] as Secretary (non-board). That the company apply for the NIF (tax ID) and commence operations upon registration. All actions necessary to effectuate these resolutions are hereby authorized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Certificate of Non-Conflict
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) – online via the official portal (www.rmc.es)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application for a negative name certificate (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social) for the proposed company name. Provide up to three alternative names. The certificate confirms no existing identical or confusingly similar name. The certificate is valid for 3 months.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, file a new application with alternative names. If the certificate is delayed, escalate via the registry's customer service or request expedited processing for an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Provisional Bank Account and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Spanish commercial bank (e.g., Banco Santander, BBVA, CaixaBank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional corporate bank account in the name of the company being formed. Deposit the minimum capital of €3,000. Obtain a certificate of deposit (Certificado de Depósito) from the bank, which must be attached to the incorporation deed. The account will be converted to a definitive account after registration.
required_dossiers: Draft incorporation deed or power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional documentation, provide the draft deed and a notarized power of attorney. If the bank refuses, choose another bank. The deposit certificate must be issued within 2 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Notario) in the jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a notary to draft the public deed of incorporation, including the bylaws (estatutos). All founding members must appear before the notary, either personally or by legal representative, to sign the deed. The deed must include the name certificate, bank deposit certificate, and details of the administrators. The notary will verify the legality and issue the deed.
required_dossiers: Proof of address of registered office (lease or title)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, correct the bylaws or provide missing documents. If the notary refuses to execute, seek a second notary. The deed must be signed within 2 months of the name certificate issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Transfer Tax (ITP) and Stamp Duty (AJD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Regional Tax Authority (Agencia Tributaria Autonómica) of the autonomous community where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 business days of the deed execution, file the deed with the regional tax authority and pay the Transfer Tax and Stamp Duty (Impuesto sobre Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados). The rate is typically 1% of the capital (varies by region). Obtain the payment receipt (Modelo 600).
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority queries the valuation, provide the deed and capital details. Late payment incurs surcharges; file a corrective declaration if errors are found.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) of the registered office province
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed, tax payment receipt, and required forms to the Provincial Commercial Registry. The registry reviews the deed for legal compliance and registers the company. Upon registration, the company acquires legal personality. The registration is published in the Official Gazette of the Commercial Registry (BORME).
required_dossiers: First copy of the incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a defect (defecto), correct the issue and resubmit within the given period (usually 15 days). If the defect is substantive, amend the deed via a notary. If the registry is slow, request expedited processing or file a complaint with the Directorate General of Registries and Notaries.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the Definitive Tax Identification Number (NIF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria – AEAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, apply for the definitive NIF (Código de Identificación Fiscal) using the provisional NIF and the registration certificate. Submit the application online or at the local AEAT office. The definitive NIF is issued immediately or within a few days.
required_dossiers: Registration certificate from the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT requests additional information, provide the registration certificate and deed. If the provisional NIF is lost, request a duplicate. The definitive NIF is essential for all tax filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Social Security and Employment Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Treasury of Social Security (Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social – TGSS) and the Provincial Labour Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with the TGSS (System of Reductions for Social Security) and obtain an employer account code (Código de Cuenta de Cotización). If hiring employees, register the employment contracts with the Public Employment Service (SEPE).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the TGSS queries the registration, provide the deed and NIF. If the employer code is delayed, follow up with the TGSS. Non-registration may result in penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business License (Licencia de Apertura) and Activity Commencement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City Council (Ayuntamiento) of the municipality where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a prior communication (Declaración Responsable) or apply for a municipal business license (Licencia de Apertura) for the specific activity (software development and EdTech services). The license is typically not required for purely administrative offices, but if physical premises are used, a license is needed. Submit the application with the deed, NIF, and a technical report on the premises.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership title of premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the license is denied, rectify the deficiencies (e.g., fire safety, accessibility) and resubmit. If the activity is exempt, obtain a written confirmation. For online-only businesses, a declaration of activity may suffice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism (Ministerio de Industria, Comercio y Turismo) – for general industrial oversight; not applicable for software-only operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – the company operates as a digital service provider without physical manufacturing. A municipal business license (Licencia de Apertura) may be required for office premises, but no industrial operating permit is needed.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico) – regional environmental authorities may also apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity is classified as a service sector (ISIC 6201) with no significant environmental impact. No EIA is required under Annex II of Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – no industrial discharges or emissions. Office operations must comply with general waste management regulations (Law 7/2022 on Waste) and energy efficiency standards (Royal Decree 56/2016).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Certificado de Protección contra Incendios) is required for office premises with a capacity over 50 persons or if the building is multi-story. Structural load inspections are not applicable for standard office use. Occupational health and safety clearance (Evaluación de Riesgos Laborales) must be conducted per Law 31/1995, and the company must register the workplace with the regional labour authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: AEAT - Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (State Tax Administration Agency) of Spain, attached to the Ministerio de Hacienda (Ministry of Finance). Electronic filing and identity portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT at sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. The portal integrates the Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores (Forms 036/037), corporate income tax returns (Form 200 and 220 for groups), quarterly VAT return (Form 303), annual VAT summary (Form 390), SII real-time VAT books, OSS/IOSS and customs (Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales) subsystems, including DUA and EORI management. The Basque Country and Navarra have autonomous tax administrations under their respective Concierto and Convenio regimes; those regimes apply only where the company's tax residence is effectively located within their territories and are outside the scope of this standard common-territory dossier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Procedure for a non-resident-owned Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL): (1) each non-resident shareholder and statutory director obtains a personal NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) from the Spanish consulate or the Comisarías de Policía; (2) secure the company name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación social) from the Registro Mercantil Central; (3) before execution of the deed, obtain a provisional corporate NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) - alphanumeric format letter + 8 digits + control character, e.g., B12345678X - by filing Form 036 at any AEAT office or electronically with digital certificate; (4) execute the public deed of incorporation before a Spanish notary, paying the regional ITP-AJD stamp duty on the capital contribution (typically 0.5%-1.5%); (5) file the deed for registration in the Registro Mercantil and concurrently register the company and directors with the Social Security system; (6) within six months of the provisional NIF, request the definitive NIF by filing the definitive census entry (Form 036), declaring the SL as an IVA (VAT) taxpayer and, if required, as an intra-community operator (VIES validation); (7) obtain electronic certificates (FNMT/Cl@ve) and open a Spanish bank account. A foreign non-resident company that itself carries out taxable supplies in Spain without a permanent establishment must also register under Form 036 and may be obliged to designate a Spanish tax representative; no fee applies to the NIF allocation itself.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The SL (sociedad de responsabilidad limitada) is a Spanish-resident capital company taxable at entity level under the Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS, Ley 27/2014) on worldwide income; there is no pass-through attribution of profit to shareholders. The standard corporate rate is 25%; a reduced 15% rate applies to newly created qualifying SMEs for the first two profitable tax periods under art. 29.1 LIS. Outbound dividends and interest to non-resident shareholders/creditors are subject to IRNR withholding (default 19%, lowered by applicable tax treaties). 'Territorial_Scope' is not the correct descriptor because Spain taxes worldwide income, though a 95% participation exemption (art. 21 LIS) applies to qualifying foreign dividends and capital gains, complemented by foreign tax credit relief (art. 31 LIS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no US-style check-the-box election; entity classification is statutory. Available elections and regimes relevant to the EdTech SL include: (1) the 15% reduced IS rate for newly formed SMEs satisfying art. 29.1 LIS conditions (automatic once requirements are met; no election form); (2) VAT simplified regime (Régimen simplificado) for taxpayers with previous-year turnover up to EUR 500,000, elected or renounced via Form 037; (3) VAT cash-accounting basis (criterio de caja) for businesses with previous-year turnover up to EUR 2,000,000, purchases up to EUR 2,000,000 and cash receipts up to EUR 1,000,000, shifting VAT chargeability to the moment of payment; (4) Spanish tax consolidation (grupo de consolidación fiscal, arts. 58-70 LIS) where the group holds at least 75% of the SL; (5) VAT group (grupo de IVA) election with AEAT authorisation; (6) Union OSS election for distance sales and B2C electronically supplied services to EU consumers, and IOSS for low-value imports; and (7) mandatory ATAD 2 anti-hybrid rules transposed by Ley 11/2021, which operate compulsorily - no elective neutralisation of hybrid mismatches is permitted under Spanish law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) - central bank, eurosystem member, operator of TARGET2-ES settlement and compiler of balance-of-payments statistics. Foreign exchange and investment control authority: Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa (Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise) through the Dirección General de Comercio Exterior e Inversiones (General Directorate of Foreign Trade and Investments), which administers the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores (Foreign Investment Registry) under Law 19/2003 and Royal Decree 571/2023. AML/CFT supervision: SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención de Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias). FX derivatives supervision: CNMV (Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores) under MiFID II.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a eurozone member state with full and unrestricted convertibility of the euro and of foreign currencies; no exchange-control or currency-rationing regime exists. Articles 63 to 65 TFEU and Law 19/2003 on capital movements and foreign economic transactions fully liberalize current account transactions - subscription licence fees, app-store settlements, royalties, cloud-hosting payments, and marketing spend - with no prior authorization, quota, or convertibility certificate requirement. The capital account is equally liberalized for SL equity subscription, shareholder loans, intragroup financing, and profit repatriation; the only formalities are ex-post statistical filing of non-resident direct investments with the Foreign Investment Registry within one month of formalization, and balance-of-payments declarations by the resident bank for transactions exceeding EUR 50,000. Profit remittance is free, subject to the 19% IRNR (non-resident income tax) withholding on dividends, reducible under applicable double tax treaties; documentary evidence of distributable reserves and tax residence is required, but no exchange-control approval applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None apply. Spain has no statutory export-proceeds surrender ratio, no mandatory repatriation timeline, and no compulsory conversion into EUR. Software and EdTech subscription exporters may lawfully retain export receivables in foreign-currency accounts maintained at resident Spanish credit institutions, convert them into EUR at their discretion, or use them directly for foreign disbursements. The sole regulatory burden is statistical: the Banco de España balance-of-payments regime requires reporting of transactions with non-residents exceeding EUR 50,000 in gross value, which in practice the receiving Spanish bank files automatically through the SDE (Sistema de Declaraciones en el Banco de España). No Ministry approval, licence, or prior declaration is needed to invoice in USD, MXN, COP, CLP, BRL, or any other currency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (multicurrency EUR/USD/MXN/COP/CLP/BRL) / Operational Business Account for treasury, payroll and FX execution
Capital Escrow Account and Multicurrency Current Account with LatAm correspondent clearing network
Operational Current Account (EUR) plus Treasury Account for app-store settlement receipts, payroll and supplier disbursements
Business Operating Account - accepts non-resident shareholders but applies enhanced due diligence and provisional transaction limits
Commercial and Treasury Account with digital onboarding capability and medium corporate appetite for international subscription treasury structures
Standard Current and Capital Account - lower appetite for cross-border digital EdTech treasury structures and non-resident UBO chains

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Operational feasibility: MEDIUM-HIGH for day-to-day treasury flows; LOW for capital escrow and equity injection accounts. Spanish-authorised electronic money institutions and payment institutions operating under Law 21/2010 and Royal Decree-Law 19/2018, as well as EU/EEA EMIs passported into Spain under PSD2 (for example Wise, Revolut, Qonto, Ponto, Payoneer, Bnext, and Mones), may lawfully provide current accounts, FX conversion of settlement funds, collections, disbursements, and expense cards for a low-risk ISIC 6201 EdTech subscription operator. However, EMIs are not credit institutions: they cannot take deposits, cannot act as escrow for equity capital contributions, are not direct members of TARGET2-ES, and must settle through Tier-1 correspondent banks. An offshore digital EMI is viable as a sweep operating rail for Apple IAP and Google Play Billing net settlements, provided it holds a valid EU e-money licence, customer funds are safeguarded under PSD2, and SEPBLAC-facing agency documentation is available. Principal constraints: transaction ceilings, refusal of high-value inbound capital wires, enhanced remote KYC for non-resident UBOs, and inability to provide NDF lines, documentary credits, or committed liquidity facilities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the practical standard but not an absolute legal mandate. Under Law 10/2010 and Royal Decree 304/2014, customer identification may be performed non-face-to-face using an advanced electronic signature or certified eIDAS digital identity, and onboarding interviews may be conducted by secure video conference where the bank's AML program permits remote onboarding. In practice, for a Spanish SL with non-resident shareholders, at least the sole administrator or one joint administrator with signatory authority must appear physically at the Spanish branch for the initial KYC interview; non-resident UBOs may be identified by video verification coupled with notarially certified passports. Corporate resolutions and powers of attorney issued abroad must be apostilled under the Hague Convention and, where necessary, translated into Spanish by a sworn translator. Where no physical attendance is possible, Tier-1 banks may open the account remotely under enhanced due diligence with a provisional transaction limit, subject to completion of the documentary file within 30 business days; a notarized power of attorney granted before a Spanish notary is generally accepted as equivalent to physical presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tier-1 compliance rejection of UBO documentation where ultimate shareholders are non-EEA residents and the corporate chain includes opacity-prone intermediate jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish UBO declaration under article 4 of Law 10/2010 identifying every natural person holding 25% or more of the SL; complete organisational chart from ultimate beneficial owners to the SL; apostilled certificates of incorporation, commercial registry extracts and good-standing certificates for each intermediate entity; certified passports and NIE documents of all natural UBOs; sworn source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statement; audit trail of the equity funding from the remitting bank accounts; notarized and apostilled power of attorney for the local account signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial equity injection of EUR 3,000 or more originating from a foreign bank account or LatAm settlement wallet, triggering mandatory SEPBLAC threshold reporting, DDP (due diligence principles) alarms, and round-trip structuring suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial escritura constitutiva or aumento de capital identifying subscribers, shares and contribution method; legalised and apostilled signatures of foreign shareholders; certification of the SL's NIF (tax identification code); twelve-month bank statements from the remitting institution evidencing source of funds; full business plan, operating budget and signed Apple/Google platform agreements demonstrating commercial purpose; auditor certificate confirming that contributions are fully paid in and booked in the equity register; corporate resolutions designating the account as wholly-owned treasury cash rather than a third-party escrow service.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction monitoring flags on high-frequency low-value app-store credits from Apple and Google in BRL, CLP, MXN and ARS, combined with immediate outbound cloud and royalty disbursements, interpreted as pass-through or layering activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Apple Developer Program and Google Play Developer agreements confirming settlement cycles and net remittance terms; monthly platform payout statements and exchange-rate reports reconciled to the SL's revenue ledger; audited revenue recognition and refund ledger; board-approved group treasury policy describing the collection-sweep and disbursement waterfall; statutory auditor certificate over cash-flow mapping; correspondence file with payment aggregators; copies of filed IS (corporate income tax), IVA (VAT) and IRNR declaration forms for the relevant period; prompt written response to the MLRO explaining the commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank refusal of a 'capital escrow account' request on the grounds that escrow services to third parties would require a payment-institution or credit-institution licence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written confirmation that the requested account is a non-interest-bearing operational equity account owned exclusively by the SL and not an escrow agency serving third parties; notarial deed and shareholder resolution designating the account as wholly-owned treasury cash; SEPA/SWIFT remittance mandate naming the SL as beneficiary; assessment of known source of funds under article 17 of Law 10/2010; auditor statement confirming that no client monies or third-party funds will be held; description of the single-purpose wiring protocol for capital subscription only.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant sequence: (i) the SL executes the incorporation or capital-increase deed before a Spanish notary and obtains the NIF; (ii) the non-resident shareholder remits funds via SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR currencies, or SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR, with field 72 referencing the escritura number, the SL's NIF, and the memo 'capital suscrito y desembolsado'; the beneficiary account name must match the SL's exact registered name to avoid misposting; (iii) the receiving Spanish bank performs OFAC and EU consolidated list sanctions screening, UBO matching, fraud checks and source-of-funds verification before crediting; (iv) the bank files the automated balance-of-payments statistical return through the SDE system and the investor files the ex-post FDI declaration with the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores through the DINA electronic platform within one month of formalization under Royal Decree 571/2023; (v) funds may be deployed only after the deed is filed in the Commercial Registry and equity is booked; for USD, BRL or other FX-denominated injections, the receiving bank executes an onshore spot conversion into EUR at the transaction-day screen rate, records the spot deal ticket, and includes the trade in its FX position records for audit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Eurozone-native clearing: SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant (SCT Inst) settle domestic and EU payroll, social security contributions, supplier P2P payments, tax remittances and Spanish-shareholder dividends with TARGET2 finality. Non-EUR commercial and intercompany disbursements are executed via SWIFT MT103 with OUR charges where the SL maintains funding; high-value or contingent international procurement is supported by documentary Commercial Letters of Credit governed by UCP 600 and standby letters of credit. App-store commission payments to Apple and Google follow the platforms' predefined net-remittance wire schedules, with EUR settlement via SEPA where the platforms hold EU treasury entities; where intercompany treasuries with LatAm operating agents exist, monthly cross-currency sweeps are executed under an ISDA-style master netting agreement with ISO 20022 pain.001/pain.002 message flows via EBICS upload to obtain transparent reconciliation and audit evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX outright forward contracts (deliverable) in EUR/MXN, EUR/COP, EUR/BRL, EUR/CLP and EUR/USD with tenors up to 12 months, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with CSA, or under the local AEB/CMOF master agreement, with MiFID II-licensed credit institutions.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) cash-settled in EUR or USD for currencies subject to convertibility or offshore-market constraints, notably the Argentine peso (ARS) and other restricted-convertibility LatAm currencies, documented under the 1998 FX and Currency Option Definitions or the 2021 ISDA definitions with fallback fixing clauses.

FX vanilla options and zero-cost collars (risk-reversals and spread collars) purchased from EU investment firms to hedge app-store payout currency risk and dividend repatriation exposure; speculative positions are excluded by the bank's suitability and appropriateness assessment.

Cross-currency swaps (XCCY) for long-term balance-sheet hedging of intragroup capital and loan positions with LatAm subsidiaries, documented under ISDA with CNMV post-trade reporting and cleared or collateralized as applicable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalization of accounting books and statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of each financial year; for a 31 December year-end, generally by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No standard fixed late fee; failure may affect evidentiary compliance and can contribute to administrative enforcement. Electronic legalization is required.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Meeting for approval of annual accounts and allocation of results
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders; no external filing authority for the meeting itself
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each financial year; for a 31 December year-end, generally by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential director liability for statutory non-compliance; delayed approval postpones the annual-accounts filing deadline and may lead to Mercantile Registry closure and administrative fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing, including management report where applicable and annual beneficial-ownership statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the annual accounts; ordinarily by 30 July where accounts are approved on 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine generally ranging from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, subject to statutory calculations; Registry closure normally begins after one year from the filing deadline and prevents registration of most subsequent corporate instruments until rectified.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, generally 1 to 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Voluntary late filing without prior notice generally triggers a surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay, or 15% after more than 12 months, plus late-payment interest; filing after notice may trigger penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding and payment-on-account information return, Form 190, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally 1 to 31 January following the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate informational filing may incur fixed penalties under the General Tax Law, with higher sanctions for repeated, incomplete, or materially inaccurate information.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit generally applies when the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets of EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover of EUR 5.7 million, or average employees of more than 50. Additional mandatory-audit rules apply to certain regulated entities, public-interest entities, grant recipients, and other statutory circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) and applicable Spanish accounting legislation. IFRS is generally not mandatory for an unlisted standalone Spanish SL; IFRS may apply to qualifying consolidated groups or where otherwise elected or required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain accurate beneficial-ownership information and report the annual beneficial-ownership statement with the annual accounts filing. Changes in beneficial ownership or control must be reflected through the applicable Mercantile Registry or Central Register procedures without waiting for the annual filing. Share transfers in an SL must be recorded in the Register of Members and documented in accordance with Spanish transfer restrictions and formalities. Spain has no separate general annual return equivalent to the United Kingdom annual confirmation statement.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and persons holding powers of attorney, where applicable
Register of Contracts with the Sole Shareholder, if the company is single-member
Accounting books and annual accounts documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 650-1,950 per year for registered-office, corporate-secretarial, and local representation support, depending on provider and service scope
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 1,500-5,000 for a small Spanish SL subject to mandatory or voluntary audit; complex, regulated, or group audits may materially exceed this range

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general Corporate Income Tax rate. Newly incorporated entities may apply 15% during the first tax period in which they obtain a positive taxable base and the following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions and anti-abuse conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly incorporated entities may qualify for the 15% rate described above. Small entities may receive reduced rates under transitional legislation, including a reduced rate for entities with qualifying prior-year net turnover below EUR 1 million. Qualifying research, development and technological innovation activities may benefit from statutory tax credits. Patent-box relief may apply to qualifying net income from eligible intangible assets. Tax credits and incentives require substantiation, statutory documentation and compatibility checks with State-aid limits. Spanish tax losses are carried forward indefinitely, subject to utilization limits generally based on prior-year net turnover: 70%, 50%, 25% or 24% of the positive taxable base, with a EUR 1 million minimum offset generally available before percentage limitations.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No statutory expiry; utilization is subject to percentage limitations, the EUR 1 million minimum offset rule and anti-avoidance restrictions on acquired-company losses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) electronic office using a digital certificate, Cl@ve where permitted, or an authorized representative. Modelo 202 is the periodic Corporate Income Tax installment-payment return. Modelo 222 applies instead of Modelo 202 for entities within a consolidated tax group.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Modelo 200: annual. Modelo 202: three installment payments annually, normally in April, October and December. Modelo 222: same payment schedule for consolidated groups.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200: within the 25 calendar days following the six months after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the normal filing window is 1 to 25 July of the following year; where payment is made by direct debit, the practical deadline is generally 20 July. Modelo 202 and Modelo 222: normally 1 to 20 April, October and December; direct-debit payment is generally available until the 15th of the relevant month.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Spanish tax identification number (NIF), registered address, tax period start and end dates, activity classification, legal form and filing type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL files using its own NIF and Spanish legal identity. Non-resident shareholders, directors and related parties are reported with their foreign tax identification and residence information where requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting assets, liabilities, equity, turnover, operating expenses, depreciation, finance income and finance costs, reconciled to statutory accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only the Spanish SL's accounting figures. Do not report the non-resident parent's worldwide accounts except where a specific related-party, group or consolidation disclosure requires them.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before Spanish Corporate Income Tax according to the approved statutory accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Spanish statutory accounting records maintained under the Spanish General Accounting Plan. Intercompany charges must be recorded consistently with the legal agreements and arm's-length analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and deductions for non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, provisions, impairment, exempt income, tax credits and other book-to-tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assess deductibility of payments to non-residents, including interest limitation, withholding compliance, beneficial ownership, anti-hybrid rules, transfer pricing and business-purpose requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of transactions with related entities and persons, transaction categories, amounts, valuation method and documentation status where required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report cross-border management services, software, platform, royalty, financing, marketing and cost-sharing transactions with the foreign group. Maintain evidence of services received and benefits obtained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting result after statutory adjustments, loss utilization and applicable exemptions or reductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Spanish-source and Spanish-resident-entity rules to the SL. A non-resident shareholder's residence does not convert the SL into a branch or permit exclusion of Spanish taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening tax losses, losses utilized in the period and closing balance, subject to percentage limitations and anti-avoidance rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Acquisition of a loss-making SL by a foreign group may restrict losses where statutory change-of-control and dormant-activity conditions are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax rate and gross tax liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable statutory or preferential rate multiplied by the taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the rate legally available to the SL for the relevant tax period; shareholder residence and treaty eligibility normally do not alter the SL's resident-company rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research and development, technological innovation, foreign tax, investment, employment and other legally available credits or deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain technical reports, invoices, payroll records, project allocation schedules and certification evidence. Foreign-parent funding does not by itself establish eligibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payments made under Modelo 202 or Modelo 222 and the resulting balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile installments to the annual liability and investigate differences caused by preferential rates, tax credits, loss utilization or withholding credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish withholding tax and prepayments suffered by the SL, supported by certificates and payment records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not credit withholding suffered by a foreign shareholder against the SL's Corporate Income Tax. Dividend, interest and royalty withholding generally belongs to the recipient's tax position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest expense, net borrowing costs, EBITDA-based limitation and disallowed interest carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document debt capacity, commercial rationale, interest rate, repayment terms, guarantees and withholding compliance for shareholder or group financing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation between the filed return, approved annual accounts, accounting books, tax adjustments and supporting schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure consistency with Registro Mercantil filings, payroll, VAT, withholding returns, Intrastat or OSS records where applicable, and group reporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bank account, direct debit or payment reference, refund account where applicable, authorized filer and electronic signature.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder or director may authorize a Spanish tax representative or advisor, but the SL remains responsible for the accuracy and timely filing of the return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing with tax payable generally attracts a surcharge of 1% plus an additional 1% for each complete month of delay up to 12 months. After 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus late-payment interest from the end of the 12-month period. A return filed after a tax authority requirement can trigger a fixed penalty generally of EUR 200, potentially reduced when statutory conditions are met, plus the tax and interest due. Incorrect returns may attract penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the improperly unpaid amount, depending on concealment, repeated conduct and other aggravating factors. Late Modelo 202 payments may generate surcharge, interest and enforcement costs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, installment payment on account of Corporate Income Tax, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic office. The standard calculation is based either on the prior-period tax liability or on the current-period tax base, depending on the taxpayer's statutory circumstances.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Normally 1 to 20 April, October and December; direct-debit payment is generally available until the 15th of the relevant month.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF, legal name, tax period and applicable installment period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's NIF and not the foreign parent's tax number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year Corporate Income Tax liability or current-year accounting and tax base, as legally applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the selected method to the prior Modelo 200, current management accounts and expected annual tax credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory percentage applied to the calculation basis, reduced by eligible credits and prior installment amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not reduce the installment for unsubstantiated foreign-group charges or unverified tax credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount payable, zero result or refund status where legally available.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain bank evidence and the electronic filing receipt.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment or filing is subject to the general Spanish surcharge, interest and enforcement regime. A tax authority notice can increase the penalty exposure and eliminate voluntary-compliance treatment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends paid by a Spanish resident company to a non-resident recipient, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. The EU Parent-Subsidiary exemption may eliminate withholding where the statutory ownership, holding-period, legal-form, subject-to-tax and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. A qualifying Spanish participation exemption may also apply at shareholder level, subject to statutory conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence issued by the recipient's foreign tax authority and verify beneficial ownership, treaty entitlement, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose requirements where relevant. The Spanish payer should retain the certificate, ownership-chain documents, board resolutions, payment records and evidence supporting the reduced rate or exemption. Apply the treaty rate at source only where documentation is sufficient. If excess tax was withheld, the non-resident generally claims a refund through Modelo 210 within the statutory limitation period, attaching the residence certificate, withholding certificate and payment evidence. Treaty eligibility does not override Spanish anti-abuse, beneficial-ownership or EU anti-avoidance rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Spanish non-resident income tax withholding is generally 24% for royalties and other qualifying income paid to non-residents outside the EU/EEA regime, with a generally 19% rate for qualifying EU/EEA recipients and certain other categories. Interest is generally subject to 19% domestic withholding. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive may provide exemption for qualifying associated EU companies, subject to minimum ownership, holding-period, legal-form, subject-to-tax and anti-abuse conditions. Tax treaties frequently reduce royalty and interest withholding to rates commonly ranging from 0% to 15%, depending on the treaty and income classification. Software access, SaaS, platform fees, technical support and digital advertising must be classified based on the contractual rights and actual functions; labeling a payment as a service does not prevent royalty withholding where a right to use intellectual property is granted.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 aggregate transaction value per related counterparty and transaction type is the principal threshold below which full transfer-pricing documentation is generally not mandatory, subject to exclusions and special rules. Documentation may still be required for transactions involving Spanish tax havens or low-tax jurisdictions, restructurings, transfers of businesses or assets, and other prescribed categories. A Local File is generally required above the applicable threshold and for material or specifically regulated transactions. A Master File is generally required where the Spanish entity forms part of a multinational group and statutory conditions apply. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain has no separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Substance is nevertheless material under Spanish transfer-pricing, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, principal-purpose, controlled foreign company, hybrid mismatch, participation exemption and treaty rules. The SL should maintain real Spanish decision-making, personnel or appropriately controlled outsourced functions, premises or operational capability, commercial risk assumption, accounting records, customer and supplier evidence, and demonstrable benefits from intra-group services. A pass-through company with nominal activity, circular financing, conduit payments or no capacity to control risks may face denial of deductions, treaty benefits or exemptions, transfer-pricing adjustments and joint liability consequences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and concealed profits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting subscription revenue, app-store receipts, advertising income or foreign customer revenue; maintaining parallel accounts; creating false expenses; or distributing undeclared profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax assessment for unpaid tax, late-payment interest and tax penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount. Serious tax fraud may constitute a criminal offense where the statutory tax-loss threshold is exceeded, with imprisonment generally from one to five years and a fine generally from one to six times the amount defrauded. Aggravated cases can attract higher imprisonment and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur civil liability for intentional or negligent tax conduct, subsidiary liability under Spanish General Tax Law provisions, restitution, asset seizure and criminal liability. A court may impose disqualification from public office or management. Travel restrictions may arise in criminal or enforcement proceedings, but are not an automatic consequence of ordinary tax delinquency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False invoices and fictitious intercompany services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging the Spanish SL for non-existent management, software, marketing, licensing or consulting services, or using invoices unsupported by personnel, deliverables, benefit or payment evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of deductions and input tax credits, transfer-pricing adjustment, withholding exposure, late-payment interest and penalties generally up to 50% to 150% of the tax shortfall. Deliberate falsification may constitute accounting or tax-document fraud and may trigger criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize or knowingly accept fictitious invoices may face civil restitution, tax subsidiary liability, criminal fines and imprisonment. Professional advisors may also face liability where they knowingly participate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's-length royalty, financing, cost-sharing, commission or service prices to shift Spanish profits to a foreign affiliate without contemporaneous functional analysis and evidence of benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment, compensating adjustment where permitted, secondary adjustment, late-payment interest and transfer-pricing documentation penalties. Failure to document or provide correct data may attract fixed penalties calculated per omitted, incorrect or incomplete data, subject to statutory caps and minimums.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil and tax liability for deliberate profit diversion and may be prosecuted where the conduct forms part of tax fraud. Ordinary transfer-pricing disagreement does not by itself establish criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Dividend, interest and royalty withholding failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying foreign shareholders or affiliates without withholding, applying treaty relief without a residence certificate, ignoring beneficial ownership, or misclassifying royalties as services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of unpaid withholding tax, late-payment interest and withholding penalties generally based on the amount not withheld or not paid. The Spanish payer may remain liable even where the foreign recipient received the gross amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil or subsidiary tax liability for deliberate failure to withhold and may face criminal exposure if the conduct is part of intentional tax fraud. The foreign recipient may also lose treaty relief and become directly assessed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorrectly classifying B2C digital language-learning services, failing to use the EU One-Stop Shop where required, omitting intra-EU sales, or treating Apple and Google settlement statements as outside the Spanish VAT perimeter without analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT assessment, late-payment interest, surcharges and penalties generally based on the unpaid or improperly credited VAT. Incorrect invoicing, record and reporting failures may generate additional fixed penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly or subsidiarily liable where they intentionally cause VAT non-compliance, frustrate collection or continue unlawful conduct after a formal notice. Criminal tax liability may arise when statutory thresholds and intent requirements are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Controlled foreign company and anti-abuse failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using foreign affiliates or low-tax entities to hold software rights, collect customer receipts, finance the Spanish SL or accumulate passive income without genuine functions, personnel, assets and risk control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inclusion of attributable income under Spanish CFC rules, denial of exemptions or treaty benefits, tax assessment, interest and penalties. Anti-abuse rules may recharacterize transactions according to their actual economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face tax subsidiary liability and, where concealment or fraudulent intent is established, criminal prosecution. Corporate separateness is not a defense to personal participation in fraudulent conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, beneficial ownership and suspicious-payment failures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing the ultimate beneficial owner, accepting unexplained third-party funding, using nominee shareholders, routing subscription proceeds through personal accounts, or failing to report suspicious transactions where the entity is subject to Spanish AML obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML violations may be classified as minor, serious or very serious and can result in significant administrative fines, public disclosure, management disqualification and restrictions on conducting regulated activities. Criminal money-laundering conduct may result in imprisonment and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, beneficial owners and compliance officers may be personally fined, disqualified or prosecuted. Asset freezing, confiscation and judicial travel restrictions may occur in criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain books, altering revenue records, backdating intercompany agreements, suppressing app-store statements, or filing accounts inconsistent with tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, accounting and corporate-law sanctions, penalties for obstruction or inaccurate filings, and potential criminal liability for falsification of commercial documents or accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil damages, creditor claims, disqualification, personal tax liability and imprisonment where accounting falsification is intentional and materially harmful.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends while insolvent, transferring intellectual property or cash to foreign affiliates for inadequate consideration, preferring related creditors, or stripping assets before a tax or creditor claim.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Clawback of transactions, director liability for insolvency deficits, creditor damages, tax recovery measures, asset seizure and criminal sanctions for insolvency-related fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to cover all or part of the insolvency deficit, lose management rights, face civil restitution and, in aggravated cases, imprisonment and criminal fines. Travel bans may be ordered by a court where legally justified.
